Do I Need Faucet Repair Service?

A faucet that leaks just 10 drips per minute can cost you more than 30 gallons per month in wasted water. That adds up on your bill! If you notice your faucet continuing to drip water after it’s shut off, have a plumber take a look. In some cases, a dripping faucet might only need a small repair like a new washer or gasket, while other issues could mean it’s time to schedule a new faucet installation.

Even if your faucet is working perfectly, you might want to upgrade. Water saving options can preserve water pressure while using less water to complete chores like doing dishes or cleaning up in the kitchen or bathroom. Kitchen faucets that turn on with a wave of your hand can help prevent cross contamination when preparing food. Added sprayers make getting caked on food off your dishes easier than ever. Talk to our plumbers about the options for upgrading your kitchen with a new faucet installation.

Upgrading your faucets can do more than just save water — it can also update the look of the room. Faucets are both functional and decorative, so you can make choices that improve the visual flow of the space. Whether you need high-arched faucets that act as a two-in-one with a sprayer, or you want something perfectly fitted for a new basin sink, we have options. Let our experienced plumbers help you choose the right water dispenser for every decor.
